autism-spectrum-disorder.scope: Diagnostic criteria, social communication deficits, repetitive behaviors, M-CHAT screening, hearing evaluation, early behavioral therapy
autism-spectrum-disorder.core: Early developmental differences combining impaired reciprocal social communication with restricted, repetitive behavior or sensory interests.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong genetic contribution, affected sibling, male sex, certain genetic syndromes
Prematurity and older parental age increase risk; vaccines do not cause autism

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor response to name, limited joint attention/pointing, absent pretend play, echolalia
Rigid routines, repetitive movements, unusually narrow interests, sensory hyperreactivity or hyporeactivity
★ **Loss of acquired language or social skills** → prompt developmental and medical evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Neurodevelopmental differences affect social reciprocity, communication, and behavioral flexibility
Intellectual ability and language level vary widely; normal intelligence does not exclude diagnosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **M-CHAT-R/F at 18 and 24 months**; developmental surveillance at every well visit
Positive screen → follow-up interview when required, comprehensive developmental evaluation; screening alone never diagnoses
★ Confirm all 3 social domains + ≥2 repetitive/restricted domains, early onset, functional impairment
**Audiology evaluation** for language delay or apparent deafness; assess cognition, adaptive skills, comorbidities
Offer chromosomal microarray and fragile X evaluation; EEG only for seizure concern or atypical regression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Early intervention referral immediately**, without awaiting definitive diagnostic testing
Individualized developmental/behavioral intervention, speech-language support, occupational services, school accommodations
Parent-mediated skill building and communication supports; target practical function and participation
Severe dangerous irritability → risperidone or aripiprazole; no drug treats core social deficits

rows.label: Complications
items: Anxiety, ADHD, epilepsy, sleep disturbance, feeding selectivity; wandering and self-injury risks
Antipsychotics → weight gain, metabolic abnormalities, movement disorders

rows.label: Prevention
items: Family genetic counseling, sibling developmental monitoring; no established primary preventive intervention
Safety planning for wandering, water exposure, and caregiver support

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hearing loss: impaired sound response without characteristic repetitive behaviors
Language disorder: preserved nonverbal reciprocity and shared interests
Social communication disorder: social-language deficits without restricted repetitive behaviors

autism-spectrum-disorder.evidence: Checked screening/early referral 2026-10-30: [AAP autism resources](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-behavioral-pediatrics-a-resource-guide-for-general-pediatricians/autism-spectrum-disorder-resources-for-pediatricians/); diagnostic criteria established DSM-5-TR teaching.

carpal-tunnel-syndrome.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
carpal-tunnel-syndrome.scope: Median nerve entrapment, pregnancy and endocrine risk factors, Phalen and Tinel tests, wrist splinting, corticosteroid injection, surgical release
carpal-tunnel-syndrome.core: Median nerve compression at the wrist causes nocturnal paresthesias in the thumb, index, middle, and radial ring fingers.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pregnancy/fluid retention, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, rheumatoid arthritis
Forceful repetitive hand activity, wrist trauma; dialysis-associated amyloid in selected patients

rows.label: Clues
items: Shaking hand relieves symptoms; driving or sustained wrist flexion aggravates symptoms
★ **Thenar weakness/atrophy**, dropping objects, impaired thumb opposition → advanced nerve injury
Central palm sensation usually spared because palmar cutaneous branch bypasses tunnel
Bilateral symptoms common; isolated little-finger symptoms argue against median neuropathy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Raised pressure beneath transverse carpal ligament → median nerve ischemia/demyelination
Long-standing compression progresses to axonal loss and persistent motor impairment

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical history + **Phalen/Tinel or carpal compression** findings support clinical diagnosis
Phalen: sustained wrist flexion; Tinel: percussion over median nerve reproduces distal paresthesia
★ **Nerve-conduction studies/EMG** for atypical presentation, severity assessment, or uncertain diagnosis before surgery
Targeted TSH/glucose testing when systemic disease suspected; routine wrist imaging unnecessary

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Mild/moderate → **neutral-position wrist splint at night**, ergonomic modification
Local corticosteroid injection for persistent symptoms or short-term relief; pregnancy often resolves postpartum
★ Severe deficit, denervation, or failed conservative care → **surgical carpal tunnel release**
NSAIDs do not relieve the underlying compression; avoid repeated ineffective analgesic-only management

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent sensory loss and thenar wasting if severe compression persists
Injection → transient hyperglycemia, rare nerve injury; surgery → scar pain or incomplete release

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reduce prolonged wrist flexion/extension and forceful vibration; adjust workstation and tools
Manage contributing endocrine/inflammatory disease; reassess worsening motor function promptly

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical radiculopathy: neck pain, dermatomal weakness/reflex changes
Ulnar neuropathy: little finger/ulnar ring symptoms, interosseous weakness
Pronator syndrome: proximal forearm pain with palmar sensory involvement

carpal-tunnel-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established peripheral nerve localization and management.

celiac-disease.name: Celiac disease
celiac-disease.scope: Gluten-sensitive enteropathy, malabsorption, iron deficiency anemia, dermatitis herpetiformis, IgA anti-tTG, small bowel villous atrophy, gluten-free diet
celiac-disease.core: Gluten-triggered autoimmune small-bowel injury causing malabsorption or unexplained iron deficiency, sometimes with intensely pruritic extensor-surface dermatitis herpetiformis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroid disease, selective IgA deficiency
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 susceptibility; positive genotype common and not diagnostic

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, weight loss; constipation or minimal GI symptoms possible
Iron deficiency refractory to oral replacement, aphthous ulcers, low bone density
Children: poor growth/delayed puberty; severe disease: hypoalbuminemia, edema, vitamin deficiencies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue transglutaminase modifies gliadin → T-cell response damages proximal intestinal mucosa
Impaired absorption → iron/folate/calcium deficiency; cutaneous granular IgA deposition causes rash

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ While **eating gluten → IgA anti-tTG + total IgA**; gluten restriction causes false negatives
★ IgA deficiency → **IgG anti-tTG or deamidated gliadin peptide antibodies**
★ Adults: positive serology or high suspicion → **EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies**, even if mucosa normal
Biopsy: villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes; high suspicion overrides negative serology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Lifelong gluten-free diet**: avoid wheat, barley, rye; dietitian, cross-contamination counseling
Pure uncontaminated oats usually tolerated; replace iron, folate, calcium, vitamin D and other measured deficiencies
Dermatitis herpetiformis: dapsone for rapid relief after G6PD testing; diet treats underlying intestinal injury
Persistent symptoms → assess gluten exposure, alternative diagnoses; refractory disease → specialist before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis, infertility; untreated disease → enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, small-bowel adenocarcinoma
Dapsone → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; restrictive diet → nutritional imbalance

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Follow **symptoms, nutritional labs, anti-tTG trend**; persistent elevation suggests gluten exposure
Bone-density assessment in adults with risk/malabsorption; test symptomatic first-degree relatives
No proven primary prevention; do not start gluten exclusion before diagnostic testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no objective malabsorption, anemia, or inflammatory injury
Giardiasis: contaminated water exposure, stool antigen/PCR positive
Pancreatic insufficiency: low fecal elastase, pancreatic risk history

cervical-cancer-screening.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
cervical-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF guidelines by age (Pap smear alone 21-29, Pap with hrHPV cotesting or hrHPV alone 30-65), screening cessation, post-hysterectomy
cervical-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk people with a cervix from age 21; age, prior results, and cervical precancer history determine testing and cessation.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Average-risk cervix present**; sexual history and HPV vaccination do not alter schedule
HIV, immunosuppression, DES exposure, prior CIN 2+ → separate surveillance pathways

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Stop after 65 only with **adequate negative prior screening** and no high-risk history
Adequate: 3 negative cytology/2 HPV-based tests over 10 years; latest within 5
Total benign hysterectomy, no CIN 2+/cancer → stop; supracervical hysterectomy → continue

rows.label: Test
items: Choose one age-specific strategy below; annual testing increases unnecessary procedures

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ **HPV 16/18 or high-grade cytology → colposcopy**; other results use prior-history risk assessment
CIN 2+ treatment → HPV-based surveillance at least 25 years, even beyond 65

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Postcoital bleeding or visible lesion → diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening interval
Under 21: no routine screening; unknown/inadequate history after 65 → continue
USPSTF 2018 final schedule below; later draft self-collection proposals do not replace final guidance

table.title: USPSTF age-based choices
rows: Primary hrHPV or cotest every 5 years

cervical-cancer-screening.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF final recommendation (2018)](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/cervical-cancer-screening); post-treatment surveillance follows established ASCCP teaching.

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Downward crossing **2 major percentile channels** → assess intake, disease, measurement error
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**, hearing/vision assessment, targeted evaluation
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Toddler tantrums → routines, calm limits, positive reinforcement; avoid rewarding demands
Head banging at sleep onset often self-soothing; assess injuries and daytime development

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable proportional smallness may be familial
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

chronic-venous-insufficiency.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
chronic-venous-insufficiency.scope: Varicose veins, stasis dermatitis, venous stasis ulcers, superficial thrombophlebitis, post-thrombotic syndrome
chronic-venous-insufficiency.core: Venous hypertension produces dependent edema, hemosiderin pigmentation, and shallow medial ankle ulcers that improve with elevation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior DVT, obesity, pregnancy, prolonged standing, older age, family history
Reduced calf-muscle pumping from immobility; previous leg trauma or venous surgery

rows.label: Clues
items: Aching/heaviness worsened by standing; varicosities, pitting swelling, preserved pedal pulses
Eczematous itching, lipodermatosclerosis, inverted champagne-bottle leg contour
★ **Irregular, exudative gaiter-region wound**; bilateral erythema without systemic illness favors stasis dermatitis
Superficial thrombophlebitis: focal erythema over a tender palpable venous cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Valve failure or outflow obstruction → reflux, capillary leakage, chronic inflammation
Post-thrombotic syndrome: residual obstruction and valvular injury following DVT

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Venous duplex ultrasound** evaluates reflux and obstruction; clinical examination often establishes diagnosis
★ **Ankle-brachial index before compression** when PAD suspected; <0.5 → avoid sustained compression
Nonhealing or atypical ulcer → biopsy for malignancy; sudden unilateral worsening → evaluate acute DVT
New superficial cord → assess clot length, proximity to deep junction, associated DVT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adequate arterial inflow → **compression bandaging/stockings + leg elevation**; walking activates calf pump
Ulcers: saline cleansing, moist absorbent dressings, debridement when needed
Stasis dermatitis: emollients plus short-course topical corticosteroid on intact inflamed skin
Symptomatic superficial reflux → endovenous ablation; moderate arterial disease → specialist-guided reduced compression
No antibiotics for colonization alone; cellulitis → systemic antibiotics; no routine diuretics without volume overload

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent ulceration, cellulitis, contact dermatitis; superficial clot can extend into deep veins
Chronic wounds rarely undergo squamous malignant transformation; new growth or bleeding warrants biopsy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight reduction, regular mobility, avoid prolonged dependent posture
Long-term compression after ulcer healing reduces recurrence; moisturize skin and treat venous reflux

rows.label: Mimics
items: Arterial ulcer: painful punched-out toes/lateral ankle, cool foot, weak pulses
Neuropathic ulcer: plantar pressure points, sensory loss, callus
Lymphedema: dorsal foot/toe swelling, later nonpitting thickened skin

table.title: Superficial thrombosis treatment
rows: Short distal segment, no high-risk features
≥5 cm long, >3 cm from deep junction

chronic-venous-insufficiency.evidence: Thrombosis checked 2026-10-30: [SVS/AVF/AVLS 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11523430/); wound care established teaching.

constipation-and-fecal-impaction.name: Constipation and fecal impaction
constipation-and-fecal-impaction.scope: Functional constipation, medication-induced constipation, fecal impaction and overflow incontinence, digital disimpaction, laxatives, fiber
constipation-and-fecal-impaction.core: Difficult, infrequent, or incomplete defecation; loose stool can represent overflow around an impacted rectal stool mass.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low fiber, immobility, dehydration, withholding, older age; childhood onset often follows painful defecation/toilet training
Opioids, anticholinergics, iron, calcium, verapamil; hypothyroidism, hypercalcemia, neurologic disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Hard/lumpy stool, straining, incomplete emptying, <3 spontaneous stools/week; frequency alone insufficient
★ **Rectal fullness, paradoxical diarrhea, fecal soiling, urinary retention** → consider impaction
★ **Bleeding, anemia, weight loss, new persistent change**, severe distension/vomiting → structural evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Slow transit increases water absorption; pelvic-floor dyssynergia prevents coordinated expulsion
Stool retention stretches rectum → reduced sensation and leakage of liquid around retained mass

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ History, drug review, abdominal examination, **digital rectal examination** for stool, masses, pelvic-floor dysfunction
No alarm findings → clinical diagnosis; targeted TSH/calcium if suspected; colonoscopy for alarms or overdue screening
Refractory despite laxatives → anorectal manometry + balloon-expulsion test; then transit studies if needed
Empty rectum does not exclude proximal impaction; obstruction concern → abdominal imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Palpable hard rectal mass → **manual disimpaction**, then enemas; proximal stool → PEG after obstruction excluded
★ Uncomplicated constipation → **fiber gradually + polyethylene glycol**; hydration if depleted, scheduled postmeal toileting
Dyssynergic defecation → pelvic-floor biofeedback; stool softener alone will not correct outlet dysfunction
Opioid-induced: stimulant + osmotic laxative; refractory → naloxegol/naldemedine after excluding bowel obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Anal fissures, hemorrhoids, prolapse, stercoral ulceration/perforation, recurrent impaction
Magnesium laxatives → hypermagnesemia in CKD; phosphate enemas → electrolyte injury, especially renal disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintenance bowel regimen after disimpaction; regular activity, adequate dietary fiber, minimize constipating drugs
Avoid bulk fiber during unresolved impaction; pediatric withholding → reward-based routine, no punishment

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS-C: recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation/stool changes
Bowel obstruction: colicky pain, vomiting, obstipation, dilated bowel
Hirschsprung: neonatal delayed meconium, distension, absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex

table.title: Escalating agents
rows: Limited efficacy; avoid relying on it

constipation-and-fecal-impaction.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA/ACG constipation guideline 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10544839/); impaction and diagnostic pathways established teaching.

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age, family history; vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval with preserved independence; MCI: objective deficit without loss of independent function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

giant-cell-arteritis.name: Giant cell arteritis
giant-cell-arteritis.scope: Giant cell arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, vision loss
giant-cell-arteritis.core: New headache with jaw claudication or visual symptoms after age 50 requires immediate glucocorticoids to prevent irreversible blindness.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, female sex, Northern European ancestry; frequently overlaps polymyalgia rheumatica
Age <50 makes this diagnosis very unlikely

rows.label: Clues
items: Scalp tenderness, abnormal temporal artery, fever, weight loss, fatigue
★ **Transient monocular loss, diplopia, or sudden painless visual loss** → ocular ischemia
PMR: bilateral shoulder/hip aching, morning stiffness >45 minutes; true muscle strength preserved

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Granulomatous inflammation of large/medium arteries → intimal proliferation and ischemic narrowing
Posterior ciliary artery involvement causes arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ESR/CRP and CBC**: inflammation, thrombocytosis, normocytic anemia support; normal markers do not fully exclude
★ **Temporal artery biopsy** confirms; skip lesions can cause false negative, so obtain adequate segment
Ultrasound halo sign useful in experienced centers; arrange testing promptly after treatment begins
Assess pulses, arm pressures, bruits; CTA/MRA for suspected aortic/branch-vessel involvement
PMR: elevated inflammatory markers, normal CK; screen all PMR patients for cranial/visual symptoms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected cranial GCA → **high-dose oral prednisone now**, before biopsy
★ Threatened or established visual loss → **IV methylprednisolone** urgently; ophthalmology consultation
Taper slowly with symptom/marker monitoring; tocilizumab can reduce steroid exposure in selected patients
Isolated PMR → lower-dose prednisone; failure to improve promptly → reconsider diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent blindness, often sequential fellow-eye involvement; stroke, aortic aneurysm/dissection
Prolonged steroids → infection, diabetes, cataracts, osteoporosis; IL-6 blockade can suppress inflammatory markers

rows.label: Prevention
items: Bone protection and fracture-risk assessment during prolonged steroids; monitor BP/glucose
Educate about recurrent visual symptoms, jaw pain, limb claudication; evaluate aorta over time

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonarteritic ischemic optic neuropathy: vascular risks, no systemic inflammatory syndrome
Myositis: objective proximal weakness, elevated CK
TMJ disease: local joint pain/clicking rather than chewing-induced ischemic fatigue

giant-cell-arteritis.evidence: Not checked online; established rheumatologic emergency and PMR management.

gout.name: Gout and crystal arthropathy
gout.scope: Acute gout, chronic gout and urate lowering, pseudogout (CPPD)
gout.core: Abrupt intensely painful inflammatory arthritis from crystal deposition; gout and CPPD require different long-term prevention despite similar flare management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gout: CKD, obesity, alcohol, purines/fructose, thiazide/loop diuretics, low-dose aspirin
CPPD: older age, joint injury, hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis, hypomagnesemia
Flares follow surgery, dehydration, illness, or changes in urate concentration

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid-onset red swollen tender joint, often overnight; fever possible
Chronic gout: tophi on ears/olecranon, erosive arthritis; recurrent flares separated by asymptomatic intervals
CPPD in younger adults → investigate associated metabolic disorders

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Crystal phagocytosis activates inflammasome/IL-1 → neutrophilic synovitis
Most hyperuricemia reflects reduced renal urate excretion rather than excessive production

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First/atypical acute monoarthritis → **arthrocentesis**, polarized microscopy, Gram stain/culture
★ **Crystals do not exclude septic arthritis**; serum urate may be normal during gout flare
Chronic imaging: punched-out defects with overhanging edges; ultrasound double-contour sign supports urate deposition

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute either crystal flare → **NSAID, colchicine, or glucocorticoid**; intraarticular steroid only after infection excluded
CKD/ulcer/anticoagulation → favor steroid; adjust colchicine for renal impairment/interactions; avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD
★ Urate lowering: **allopurinol first-line**, including CKD; start low, titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL
Continue urate lowering during flares; may start during treated flare; no routine asymptomatic-hyperuricemia treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Gout: destructive arthritis, uric-acid stones; CPPD: chronic degenerative/inflammatory arthropathy
Allopurinol hypersensitivity; colchicine → diarrhea/neuromyopathy
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors + azathioprine/6-MP → severe marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Urate lowering: **tophi, joint damage, ≥2 flares/year**; first flare with CKD ≥3/stones/urate >9 → consider
Starting urate lowering → colchicine/NSAID prophylaxis 3–6 months; serial urate monitoring
Weight reduction, limit alcohol/fructose; replace thiazide with losartan when feasible; retain indicated aspirin
Before allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 testing with Southeast Asian/African American ancestry; CPPD lacks crystal-depleting drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: positive culture, bacteremia risk; aspiration essential when uncertain
Cellulitis: superficial inflammation, less restriction of passive joint motion
RA: persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis

gout.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACR gout guideline 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10563586/), [ACR gout education 2025](https://rheumatology.org/patients/gout); CPPD established teaching.

hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.scope: Bird fancier lung, farmer lung, acute vs chronic presentation, antigen avoidance, centrilobular ground-glass nodules on HRCT, systemic corticosteroids
hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.core: Immune-mediated small-airway and interstitial lung disease follows inhaled antigen exposure; identifying and removing the exposure is central to treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Bird proteins from pets, feathers, droppings; moldy hay in farming
Damp buildings, contaminated humidifiers/hot tubs, occupational organic dust; ask about home and hobbies

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Recurrent **cough, dyspnea, fever hours after exposure**, improvement away from source
Chronic exposure: insidious exertional limitation, weight loss, dry inspiratory crackles; clubbing with fibrosis
Hypoxemia, tachypnea, falling exercise saturation indicate substantial impairment; chronic disease may lack febrile episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Repeated antigen inhalation triggers immune-complex and T-cell responses around bronchioles and alveoli
Persistent inflammation produces poorly formed noncaseating granulomas and potentially irreversible fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Exposure history + HRCT**: centrilobular ground-glass nodules, mosaic attenuation, expiratory air trapping
Fibrotic disease: reticulation, traction bronchiectasis ± honeycombing; distribution can differ from basal-predominant IPF
PFTs: restriction and ↓DLCO, sometimes mixed obstruction; BAL lymphocytosis supports diagnosis
Serum antigen-specific IgG documents sensitization, **not disease**; absence does not exclude
Multidisciplinary review; biopsy only when exposure, imaging, and BAL leave clinically important uncertainty

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Complete antigen avoidance** and environmental remediation; respirator alone may be insufficient
★ Severe symptomatic nonfibrotic disease → **systemic glucocorticoids** to accelerate recovery
Oxygen for hypoxemia, pulmonary rehabilitation; progressive fibrotic disease → specialist antifibrotic consideration
Advanced refractory fibrosis → lung transplant evaluation; antibiotics do not treat sterile immune inflammation

rows.label: Complications
items: Progressive fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, chronic respiratory failure, cor pulmonale
Symptoms can persist despite avoidance once irreversible structural damage has occurred

rows.label: Prevention
items: Remove birds/mold sources, maintain ventilation, control workplace organic-dust exposure
Counsel household members about ongoing feather products or hidden dampness; monitor lung function after removal

rows.label: Mimics
items: IPF: older adult, basal subpleural honeycombing, no explanatory antigen
Sarcoidosis: well-formed granulomas, hilar adenopathy, extrapulmonary involvement
Organic dust toxic syndrome: heavy exposure, acute flu-like illness without antigen-specific sensitization

hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.evidence: Not checked online; established ATS diagnostic and management teaching.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.scope: Hashimoto thyroiditis, subclinical hypothyroidism, myxedema coma, autoimmune associations, levothyroxine dosing, TSH monitoring
hypothyroidism.core: Insufficient thyroid hormone slows metabolism, causing fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, and delayed reflex relaxation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hashimoto autoimmunity, thyroid surgery/radioiodine, iodine deficiency/excess
Lithium, amiodarone, postpartum thyroiditis; pituitary surgery/radiation or mass

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight gain, bradycardia, hoarseness, heavy menses, hyperlipidemia; hyponatremia in severe disease
★ **Hypothermia, altered mentation, hypoventilation, hypotension** → myxedema coma
Autoimmune clustering: type 1 diabetes, pernicious anemia, adrenal insufficiency, celiac disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced hormone activity lowers thermogenesis and cardiac output; glycosaminoglycan deposition produces nonpitting edema
Hashimoto: lymphocytic destruction; anti-TPO antibodies support autoimmune cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH and free T4** establish hormone deficiency and localize the level of dysfunction
Positive anti-TPO predicts progression from subclinical disease; ultrasound unnecessary without nodule/goiter concern
Recheck mild isolated TSH elevation after transient illness resolves; exclude medication interference

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Levothyroxine**; healthy young adult approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day; older/CAD start 12.5–25 mcg/day
Take fasting; separate calcium/iron; reassess TSH about 6–8 weeks after changes
Central disease: titrate using free T4; evaluate/replace cortisol before thyroid hormone
Subclinical: generally treat TSH ≥10; consider symptoms, antibodies, pregnancy at lower values
★ Myxedema: **IV levothyroxine + IV hydrocortisone**, airway support, cautious fluids/passive warming; treat trigger

rows.label: Complications
items: Dyslipidemia, infertility, pericardial effusion, neuropathy; severe disease → respiratory failure
Excess replacement → AF, angina, bone loss; rapid correction in CAD can precipitate ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Pregnancy: early **TSH monitoring**, usually increase existing replacement promptly; use pregnancy-specific targets
Monitor stable replacement at least annually; address adherence/absorption before escalating doses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Depression: mood symptoms without thyroid biochemical pattern
Euthyroid sick syndrome: acute systemic illness, often low T3; avoid routine hormone replacement

hypothyroidism.evidence: Not checked online; established thyroid replacement and endocrine emergency teaching.

infective-endocarditis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis.scope: Native and prosthetic valve endocarditis, Duke criteria, prophylaxis, IV drug use endocarditis, blood culture diagnostic criteria
infective-endocarditis.core: Persistent bacteremia with valve infection causes systemic emboli, valve destruction, and immune-complex injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis, congenital valve abnormality, intracardiac device
Injection drug use → tricuspid involvement; healthcare exposure, indwelling vascular access

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, new regurgitant murmur, embolic stroke, splenic infarct, hematuria
Janeway lesions painless; Osler nodes painful; splinter hemorrhages nonspecific
★ **New conduction block** → periannular abscess; right-sided disease → septic pulmonary emboli

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury → platelet-fibrin nidus → microbial adherence and vegetation
Immune complexes → glomerulonephritis; infected fragments disseminate through downstream circulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Three blood-culture sets before antibiotics**; separate peripheral draws unless resuscitation would be delayed
Major microbiology: **typical organism in ≥2 culture sets**, nontypical in ≥3; specialized serology/PCR also qualifies
★ **TTE → TEE** if prosthesis/high suspicion; major imaging: vegetation, abscess, perforation, new significant regurgitation
Definite clinical Duke: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria
Minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, nondiagnostic microbiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for acutely ill/healthcare-associated cases; tailor to cultures and setting
MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin; susceptible viridans streptococci → ceftriaxone
Prolonged pathogen-directed IV antibiotics; prosthetic infections need specialist regimen and early surgical evaluation
Surgery: heart failure, abscess, persistent bacteremia, fungal infection, or selected recurrent/large embolizing vegetations

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute regurgitation, heart failure, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection
Antibiotic nephrotoxicity, line infection; hemorrhage into embolic cerebral lesions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dental **amoxicillin** for prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, selected cyanotic/residual CHD, transplant valvulopathy
Good oral hygiene, sterile access; no routine prophylaxis for GI/GU procedures or isolated MVP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: cancer/autoimmune disease, sterile cultures
Atrial myxoma: positional obstruction, intracavitary mass; vasculitis: no infected vegetation

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate, reason, communicate choice**; specific to decision, fluctuating
Competence: legal determination; diagnosis, age, or disagreement alone does not establish incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, including life-saving treatment; avoid coercion or abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no available surrogate/directive → implied consent for necessary treatment
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or substantially changed risk → renewed consent discussion

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

insomnia.name: Insomnia
insomnia.scope: Chronic insomnia, sleep hygiene, stimulus control therapy, sleep restriction, delayed sleep-wake phase disorder, pharmacotherapy indications
insomnia.core: Persistent difficulty sleeping despite adequate opportunity, with daytime impairment, calls for CBT-I and evaluation of perpetuating causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Stress, depression/anxiety, chronic pain, irregular schedules, conditioned worry about sleep
Caffeine, alcohol, nicotine, stimulants, glucocorticoids; older age and menopause

rows.label: Clues
items: Difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep or early awakening, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability
★ Chronic disorder: **≥3 nights/week for ≥3 months**, with adequate sleep opportunity
Delayed phase: late sleep/wake times but normal sleep quality and duration when schedule unrestricted
Loud snoring, witnessed apnea, irresistible sleepiness, or restless legs suggests another sleep disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cognitive/physiologic hyperarousal and learned bed–wake association perpetuate insomnia
Circadian phase delay misaligns internal timing with required social schedule

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sleep history and 1–2-week diary**; review schedule, substances, mood, pain, and medications
Polysomnography: suspected apnea, limb movements, unusual behaviors, or refractory uncertainty; not routine
Actigraphy can clarify circadian timing; assess bipolar disorder before sleep-restriction interventions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CBT-I first-line**: stimulus control, sleep restriction/compression, cognitive restructuring, relaxation
Stimulus control: bed only for sleep/sex; leave when persistently awake, return when sleepy
Restrict time in bed to consolidate sleep, then expand; fixed wake time and avoid naps
★ **Sleep hygiene alone insufficient**; reduce evening stimulants, alcohol, screens; dark quiet room
Short-term adjunct when needed: low-dose doxepin, ramelteon, orexin antagonist, or selected Z-drug; reassess benefit/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Impaired driving/work performance, mood deterioration; hypnotics → falls, cognitive impairment, dependence
Z-drugs can cause complex sleep behaviors; avoid sedative combinations and routine antihistamines in older adults

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain regular wake time and daytime activity; address pain/mood disorders and relapse triggers
★ Delayed phase → **morning bright light + timed evening melatonin**, gradual schedule advance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Insufficient sleep: inadequate opportunity, improves with longer sleep duration
Mania: reduced need for sleep with increased energy, rather than distressing fatigue
OSA: sleep fragmentation with snoring/apneas; coexistence possible

interstitial-cystitis.name: Interstitial cystitis
interstitial-cystitis.scope: Bladder pain syndrome, chronic pelvic pain relieved by voiding, urinary urgency and frequency, Hunner lesions on cystoscopy, dietary triggers, pentosan polysulfate, behavioral modification
interstitial-cystitis.core: Bladder-associated pain worsens with filling and improves after voiding, with urinary frequency but repeatedly negative infection testing.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: More common in women; associated chronic pelvic pain, fibromyalgia, IBS
Symptoms may flare with stress, intercourse, menstruation, acidic foods, caffeine, or alcohol

rows.label: Clues
items: Suprapubic pressure/discomfort, urgency, nocturia; often small voided volumes and dyspareunia
★ **Symptoms >6 weeks**, sterile cultures, no alternate explanation support bladder pain syndrome
Patients void to relieve discomfort rather than primarily to prevent urge incontinence
Fever, flank pain, gross hematuria, weight loss → evaluate other disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heterogeneous urothelial dysfunction, neural sensitization, and pelvic-floor muscle abnormalities generate chronic pain
Hunner-lesion subtype includes focal inflammatory mucosal injury; absence of lesions does not exclude disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **History, pelvic examination, urinalysis/culture**; review pain/voiding diary and check residual when retention suspected
Hematuria or cancer risk → malignancy evaluation rather than presumptive diagnosis
Cystoscopy when uncertain or suspect Hunner lesions; not required for every uncomplicated presentation
Glomerulations are nonspecific; potassium sensitivity testing is not recommended

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Education, trigger elimination, bladder training, stress management**; individualized multimodal treatment
Pelvic-floor tenderness → **manual physical therapy**; avoid strengthening/Kegel exercises when hypertonic
Persistent symptoms: selected amitriptyline, cimetidine, hydroxyzine, or intravesical lidocaine/heparin
★ **Pentosan polysulfate may cause pigmentary maculopathy**; discuss limited benefit and arrange retinal monitoring
Hunner lesions → cystoscopic fulguration or triamcinolone injection; refractory severe disease → specialist interventions

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, sexual dysfunction, anxiety/depression, substantial quality-of-life impairment
Rare advanced fibrotic low-capacity bladder; treatments may cause sedation, anticholinergic effects, or retention

rows.label: Prevention
items: Identify individual dietary triggers; avoid unnecessary repeated antibiotics with negative cultures
Plan flare management and regular reassessment; no established primary-prevention strategy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Overactive bladder: urgency/incontinence predominates without filling-related pain
UTI: positive culture; bladder cancer: hematuria, risk factors, abnormal cystoscopy
Endometriosis: cyclic pelvic pain with gynecologic features

knee-injuries.name: Knee injuries
knee-injuries.scope: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear, posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tear, collateral ligaments, meniscal tears, knee dislocation, popliteal artery injury, Ottawa knee rules
knee-injuries.core: Knee trauma assessment starts with neurovascular safety and fracture risk, then uses mechanism, effusion timing, and targeted ligament or meniscal tests.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pivoting/cutting sports, contact trauma, dashboard impact, hyperextension
Older age, osteoporosis, and inability to bear weight increase fracture probability

rows.label: Clues
items: Immediate large effusion suggests hemarthrosis; delayed swelling and catching suggest meniscal injury
★ **Gross deformity or spontaneously reduced dislocation** → popliteal artery injury risk
Cool foot, weak pulses, paresthesia, escalating pain → vascular compromise or compartment syndrome

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ligament disruption → instability; displaced meniscal fragment → mechanical locking
Knee dislocation may stretch/tear popliteal artery despite restored alignment and initially palpable pulses

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Neurovascular examination before and after reduction**; ABI assesses arterial injury
★ ABI **<0.9 or abnormal pulses → CT angiography**; hard ischemic signs → immediate vascular intervention
Normal ABI/pulses after dislocation → serial vascular checks, not immediate discharge
Ottawa: age ≥55, isolated patellar/fibular-head tenderness, flexion <90°, or inability four-step weight-bearing → radiographs
MRI for soft-tissue injury after fracture evaluation; locked knee → prompt orthopedic assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Dislocation → **urgent reduction**, immobilization, orthopedic/vascular consultation
Initial sprain → ice/compression, analgesia, protected weight bearing then early rehabilitation
Isolated collateral sprain → hinged brace + rehabilitation; many PCL injuries managed nonoperatively
ACL rupture with athletic demands/persistent instability or combined injury → reconstruction discussion
Displaced locked meniscal tear → arthroscopy; degenerative tears without locking usually exercise-based rehabilitation

rows.label: Complications
items: Missed arterial injury → limb loss; peroneal nerve injury → foot drop
Chronic instability, recurrent meniscal injury, posttraumatic osteoarthritis, stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Neuromuscular landing/pivot training, strength and balance rehabilitation before sport return

rows.label: Mimics
items: Patellar dislocation: lateral patellar displacement, often spontaneous reduction
Septic arthritis: atraumatic hot effusion, fever; urgent aspiration

knee-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic trauma and Ottawa knee principles.

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, clubbing, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

motivational-interviewing.name: Motivational interviewing
motivational-interviewing.scope: Stages of change (precontemplation, contemplation, action), developing discrepancy, change talk, rolling with resistance
motivational-interviewing.core: Collaborative counseling that strengthens a patient’s own reasons and confidence for change by exploring ambivalence without confrontation.

rows.label: Definition
items: OARS: open questions, affirmations, reflective listening, summaries
Patient expertise and autonomy guide goals; clinician supplies information with permission

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Change talk**: desire, ability, reasons, need, commitment; invite elaboration and reflect it
Sustain talk expresses reasons to continue; discord signals need to change counseling approach

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ **Ask readiness and confidence**, explore barriers; scale questions uncover why scores are not lower
Develop discrepancy between stated values and behavior using patient observations
★ **Roll with resistance**: acknowledge perspective, reflect ambivalence, offer choices rather than argue

rows.label: Compare
items: Ask–provide–ask: elicit knowledge, share concise information, invite interpretation
Maintenance: reinforce gains, anticipate triggers; recurrence → revisit goals without shame

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Avoid the righting reflex**: lectures, scare tactics, unsolicited commands provoke defensiveness
Agreement with clinician is not commitment; obtain a patient-selected next step
Stage of change can vary by behavior and over time

motivational-interviewing.evidence: Established behavioral counseling principles; no guideline-dependent thresholds.

nonsteroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs.name: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
nonsteroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs.scope: COX-1 and COX-2 inhibition mechanism, renal adverse effects (sodium retention, acute kidney injury), gastrointestinal toxicity, cardiovascular risks
nonsteroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs.core: NSAIDs reduce pain, inflammation, and fever through cyclooxygenase inhibition, with gastrointestinal, renal, and cardiovascular tradeoffs.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Pain, dysmenorrhea, renal colic, gout; **lowest effective dose, shortest duration**
Topical diclofenac for localized joint pain reduces systemic exposure

rows.label: Mechanism
items: COX-1: gastric/platelet/renal effects; COX-2: inflammatory prostaglandins and endothelial prostacyclin
Most reversibly inhibit enzymes; aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ **Afferent arteriolar constriction** → AKI, hyperkalemia, sodium retention, hypertension/HF worsening
★ Gastritis, **ulcer/bleeding**; platelet inhibition except with selective COX-2 agents
MI/stroke risk; interstitial nephritis, analgesic nephropathy; bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma

rows.label: Avoid
items: Active GI bleeding, severe CKD, decompensated HF, peri-CABG setting
Pregnancy ≥20 weeks generally avoid; later gestation → ductal closure and fetal renal injury
Aspirin in children with viral illness → Reye syndrome

rows.label: Interactions
items: ★ ACE inhibitor/ARB + diuretic + NSAID → **high AKI risk**
Anticoagulants/antiplatelets → bleeding; NSAIDs can increase lithium and methotrexate exposure

rows.label: Monitor
items: BP, edema, creatinine, K; assess melena/anemia and prior ulcer history
High GI risk → consider PPI; reassess need rather than automatically continuing indefinitely

rows.label: Traps
items: Celecoxib reduces GI/platelet effects but retains renal and thrombotic risks
Prescribed low-dose aspirin for obstetric indications remains an exception to pregnancy NSAID restriction
Do not combine multiple NSAIDs for additional analgesia

nonsteroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs.evidence: Pregnancy safety checked 2026-10-30: [FDA NSAID warning](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-recommends-avoiding-use-nsaids-pregnancy-20-weeks-or-later-because-they-can-result-low-amniotic); other pharmacology: established teaching.

opioid-prescribing-and-safety.name: Opioid prescribing and safety
opioid-prescribing-and-safety.scope: Chronic opioid therapy, prescription drug monitoring, opioid tapering, misuse risk assessment, managing refill requests, naloxone co-prescribing
opioid-prescribing-and-safety.core: Use opioids only when expected functional benefit exceeds harm, with shared goals, ongoing reassessment, and a plan for safer prescribing.

rows.label: Principle
items: Chronic pain: prefer nonopioid options; individualize benefit–harm assessment without rigid dose ceilings
CDC outpatient guideline excludes sickle-cell pain, cancer treatment, palliative and end-of-life care

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Before starting: **PDMP, substance-use/mental-health review**, functional goals, risk discussion
Immediate-release, lowest effective dose; reassess at 1–4 weeks after starting/escalating, then regularly
★ **Offer naloxone**: overdose risk with prior overdose, OUD, apnea, benzodiazepines, higher doses

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid opioid–benzodiazepine combinations when possible; discuss alcohol and driving impairment
Never dismiss/prescribe solely from risk score, urine result, or early refill request

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Refill concern → **nonjudgmental review**, PDMP; assess withdrawal, pain, misuse/diversion
Harms exceed benefits → collaborative taper; imminent overdose danger → urgent intervention
Opioid-use disorder → offer buprenorphine/methadone; continue pain care and arrange treatment support

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No abrupt forced discontinuation**; individualized taper may take months/years
Toxicology testing supports safety, not punishment; confirm unexpected findings and assay limitations
Physical dependence/tolerance alone during supervised treatment does not establish opioid-use disorder

panic-disorder.name: Panic disorder
panic-disorder.scope: Panic attack criteria, unexpected recurrent attacks, agoraphobia, acute abortive therapy, maintenance therapy, medical rule-outs
panic-disorder.core: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks followed by at least 1 month of fear of recurrence or maladaptive behavioral change establish panic disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young adulthood, family history, trauma, anxiety sensitivity
Caffeine, stimulants, cannabis, decongestants, hyperthyroidism, withdrawal can provoke paniclike symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Abrupt intense fear peaks within minutes; palpitations, dyspnea, chest pain, paresthesias, derealization
Attack requires ≥4 characteristic symptoms; fear of dying/losing control common
★ **Syncope, exertional onset, hypoxemia, focal findings**, sustained arrhythmia → medical cause until evaluated
Agoraphobia: fear/avoidance of ≥2 situations where escape/help seems difficult, persisting ≥6 months

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Threat-circuit overactivation and catastrophic interpretation of benign sensations amplify autonomic symptoms
Hyperventilation lowers CO₂ → lightheadedness, distal tingling; avoidance reinforces anticipatory fear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis after medical/substance review**; unexpected episodes distinguish disorder from predictable triggers
Vital signs, examination, ECG for cardiopulmonary symptoms; glucose/TSH or toxicology guided by history
Chest pain risk → ACS/PE evaluation rather than automatic psychiatric attribution
Assess depression, suicidality, substance use; agoraphobia may be diagnosed separately

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ During attack → **calm reassurance, slow breathing**, reduce stimulation after excluding danger
Severe acute episode → short-term lorazepam when needed; avoid with sedatives or substance-use risk
★ Maintenance → **CBT with interoceptive exposure and/or SSRI**, such as sertraline
Start SSRI low, titrate slowly; benefit takes weeks; venlafaxine alternative
Continue effective treatment after remission, then gradual taper; benzodiazepines not preferred long-term

rows.label: Complications
items: Agoraphobic avoidance, impaired function, depression, self-medication with alcohol
Benzodiazepine dependence/withdrawal; SSRIs may initially increase anxiety

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reduce caffeine/stimulants**, regular sleep/exercise, practice exposure and relapse-prevention skills
No paper-bag rebreathing: unrecognized hypoxemia or medical illness may worsen

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent tremor, heat intolerance, low TSH
SVT: documented abrupt regular tachycardia, not solely subjective palpitations
Social anxiety: fear tied to scrutiny rather than unexpected attacks

panic-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established DSM-5-TR and anxiety treatment teaching.

pediatric-exanthems.name: Pediatric exanthems
pediatric-exanthems.scope: Measles (rubeola), rubella (German measles), roseola infantum (HHV-6), erythema infectiosum (parvovirus B19 fifth disease), scarlet fever, varicella, clinical appearance, complications
pediatric-exanthems.core: Fever with a childhood rash: use fever timing, rash progression, mucosal findings, immunization status, and pregnancy exposure to distinguish causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Incomplete immunization, daycare/school exposure, travel; immunosuppression increases severe viral disease
Pregnant contacts require prompt assessment after rubella, parvovirus, or varicella exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Toxic appearance**, petechiae/purpura, hypotension, meningismus → evaluate invasive infection immediately
Measles: cough, coryza, conjunctivitis precede rash; rubella: posterior auricular/suboccipital adenopathy
Varicella: trunk/scalp predominance; oral mucosal lesions may accompany the skin eruption

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Parvovirus suppresses erythroid precursors; congenital infection can cause severe fetal anemia
VZV remains latent in sensory ganglia; HHV-6 commonly causes febrile illness in infants

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected measles → **airborne isolation**, notify public health; respiratory PCR plus serum IgM
Scarlet fever → rapid GAS test; negative pediatric test → throat culture
Typical roseola/fifth disease: clinical; atypical vesicles → VZV PCR; rubella → public-health serology/PCR

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Scarlet fever → **penicillin or amoxicillin**; other uncomplicated exanthems generally supportive
Measles → hydration, complication care, clinician-supervised vitamin A for children
Severe/immunocompromised varicella → **IV acyclovir**; avoid aspirin in children

rows.label: Complications
items: Measles: pneumonia, encephalitis, delayed SSPE; rubella: congenital cataracts, deafness, PDA
Parvovirus: aplastic crisis, hydrops; roseola: febrile seizures
Varicella: bacterial superinfection, pneumonia, cerebellitis; GAS: rheumatic fever, glomerulonephritis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **MMR and varicella vaccines**; live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy and severe immunosuppression
Measles exposure: MMR within 72 hours or immune globulin within 6 days for eligible contacts

rows.label: Mimics
items: Kawasaki disease: ≥5 days fever, conjunctivitis, oral/extremity changes
Drug eruption: medication exposure without characteristic infectious sequence

table.title: Signature rash
rows: Koplik spots; face → downward confluent rash
Sandpaper rash, Pastia lines, strawberry tongue

pharyngitis.name: Pharyngitis
pharyngitis.scope: Centor score, Group A Streptococcus, rapid antigen detection, throat culture, viral pharyngitis, penicillin, peritonsillar abscess
pharyngitis.core: Most sore throats are viral; identify patients needing group A streptococcal testing and recognize deep-space infection or airway danger.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: School-age children, close contacts, crowded settings, winter/spring; GAS uncommon below age 3
Smoking, immunosuppression, incomplete vaccination broaden infectious differential

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Cough, rhinorrhea, conjunctivitis, oral ulcers** favor viral cause; avoid unnecessary GAS testing
Centor: fever, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes, absence of cough; 1 point each
McIsaac modifies by age; scoring estimates testing need, never proves bacterial infection
★ **Trismus, muffled voice, unilateral bulge, uvular deviation** → peritonsillar abscess

rows.label: Pathophys
items: GAS pharyngeal infection can trigger immune-mediated rheumatic fever or glomerulonephritis
Peritonsillar infection progresses into localized pus; deeper spread threatens airway and vessels

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ No clear viral syndrome and elevated clinical score → **rapid antigen test or NAAT**
Negative rapid antigen in symptomatic child ≥3 → throat culture; adults usually need no backup
Positive test with compatible illness → treat; asymptomatic carriage generally needs no eradication
Abscess usually clinical; ultrasound/contrast neck CT if uncertain or deep-space extension suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Confirmed GAS → **penicillin or amoxicillin for 10 days**; IM benzathine penicillin if adherence uncertain
Penicillin allergy: cephalexin if nonimmediate; azithromycin/clindamycin if immediate, accounting for local resistance
Viral illness → fluids, acetaminophen/ibuprofen; no antibiotics
★ Peritonsillar abscess → **drainage + amoxicillin-clavulanate**; airway assessment, IV ampicillin-sulbactam if severe

rows.label: Complications
items: Rheumatic fever prevented by timely GAS antibiotics; poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis not reliably prevented
Retropharyngeal spread, airway obstruction; Fusobacterium → internal jugular thrombophlebitis/Lemierre syndrome

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene; remain home until afebrile and ≥12–24 hours after effective GAS antibiotics
Do not routinely test asymptomatic household contacts or obtain test-of-cure

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV: posterior nodes, splenomegaly, amoxicillin-associated rash
Epiglottitis: drooling, tripod posture, stridor; avoid provocative throat examination
Diphtheria: adherent gray membrane, incomplete vaccination

physician-patient-communication.name: Physician-patient communication
physician-patient-communication.scope: Medical interpreters, limited English proficiency, delivering bad news, empathetic communication, family requests to withhold information
physician-patient-communication.core: Respect autonomy through understandable, honest, empathic dialogue; identify what patients understand and want before sharing decisions or sensitive information.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality, cultural humility, informed choice; language barriers never imply impaired capacity
Patient preferences determine family involvement and desired level of disclosure

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Qualified medical interpreter**, free to patient; speak directly to patient in short segments
★ Bad news: privacy → understanding/preferences → warning → plain disclosure → empathy → plan
Validate emotion; open questions, silence, teach-back; explore beliefs before correcting misinformation

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid jargon, false reassurance, interrupting, arguing, blaming, or premature advice
Avoid routine reliance on children/family for interpreting consent or sensitive discussions
Avoid promising cure or confidentiality beyond legal limits

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ **Family requests nondisclosure → ask patient privately**; patient preferences control disclosure
Capable patient may decline details or designate another recipient; document preference
Emergency without interpreter → temporary available help while securing qualified interpretation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Therapeutic privilege is narrow**; anticipated distress alone never justifies withholding diagnosis
Anger → acknowledge concern, clarify cause, establish boundaries if threatening; no reflex discharge
Requested adult-family interpreter → verify suitability/privacy/voluntariness; offer professional

physician-patient-communication.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [HHS interpreter guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/civil-rights/for-individuals/faqs/may-an-lep-person-use-a-family-member-as-an-interpreter/index.html); established autonomy and bad-news communication principles.

salivary-gland-disorders.name: Salivary gland disorders
salivary-gland-disorders.scope: Acute suppurative sialadenitis, sialolithiasis, mumps parotitis, salivary tumors
salivary-gland-disorders.core: Salivary swelling may reflect infection, obstructed flow, viral parotitis, or a neoplasm; meal association, duct drainage, and focality guide the branch.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, postoperative state, poor oral hygiene, anticholinergic drugs reduce salivary flow
Submandibular gland predisposed to stones; unvaccinated close-contact exposure favors mumps
Prior radiation and smoking increase selected salivary tumor risks; older age raises neoplasm concern

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Purulence from Stensen or Wharton duct** supports acute bacterial sialadenitis
Painful unilateral gland with fever; airway symptoms, trismus, toxic appearance → deep infection/abscess
★ **Facial weakness, fixation, rapid growth**, cervical nodes with parotid mass → malignancy warning
Dry eyes/dry mouth and recurrent bilateral swelling suggest autoimmune sicca disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis permits ascending oral bacteria; S aureus common in suppurative infection
Ductal calculus blocks secretion; mumps causes viral gland inflammation; most parotid tumors benign

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Examine oral ducts and facial nerve; **ultrasound** first for stone or focal gland lesion
Contrast CT for abscess/deep extension; culture expressed pus if present
Mumps suspicion → buccal swab RT-PCR, public health notification; serology supplements selected cases
★ Persistent solid mass → **fine-needle aspiration**, imaging and ENT assessment; avoid open diagnostic biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suppurative disease → **hydration, warm compresses, gland massage, sialogogues + amoxicillin-clavulanate**
Systemic toxicity/poor oral intake → admit, IV ampicillin-sulbactam; abscess → drainage
Obstruction → stimulate flow and remove persistent stone via sialendoscopy or selected surgery
Mumps → analgesia/hydration, isolate through 5 days after swelling onset; no antibiotic benefit
Tumor → specialist surgical excision; avoid simple enucleation of pleomorphic adenoma

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, deep neck infection, recurrent sialadenitis; parotid surgery → facial nerve injury, gustatory sweating
Mumps → orchitis, meningitis, pancreatitis, hearing loss; longstanding pleomorphic adenoma may transform

rows.label: Prevention
items: Oral hygiene, hydration, minimize xerogenic drugs; MMR vaccination for mumps prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dental abscess: focal tooth tenderness, odontogenic collection
Sjögren syndrome: chronic sicca, autoimmune features rather than acute ductal pus

table.title: Presentation patterns
rows: Older smoker; sometimes bilateral parotid masses

salivary-gland-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established salivary disease and mumps isolation teaching.

scrotal-masses.name: Scrotal masses
scrotal-masses.scope: Varicocele, hydrocele, spermatocele, testicular cancer differential, physical examination, scrotal Doppler ultrasound
scrotal-masses.core: Painless scrotal swelling requires localization: solid intratesticular lesions are malignant until proven otherwise; many extratesticular lesions are benign.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Testicular cancer: cryptorchidism, prior cancer, family history, younger adult age
Hydrocele: infancy/patent processus vaginalis, trauma, infection; varicocele from venous drainage anatomy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Firm nontransilluminating intratesticular mass** → urgent malignancy assessment
Dull ache/heaviness may occur without acute inflammation; gynecomastia suggests hormone-secreting germ-cell tumor
New isolated right-sided varicocele or failure to decompress supine → evaluate retroperitoneal obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Patent processus vaginalis permits peritoneal-scrotal communication; epididymal duct obstruction forms retention cysts
Pampiniform venous reflux raises local temperature, potentially impairing spermatogenesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Scrotal Doppler ultrasound** localizes intra-/extratesticular lesion and assesses blood flow
Examine standing/supine, with Valsalva; determine whether testis separately palpable and mass transilluminates
Suspected tumor → AFP, beta-hCG, LDH before surgery; staging CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as needed
Normal markers do not exclude malignancy; AFP elevation excludes pure seminoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspicious testicular mass → **radical inguinal orchiectomy**; avoid transscrotal biopsy
Offer sperm banking before cancer treatment; subsequent surveillance/chemotherapy/radiation depends on histology/stage
Small asymptomatic hydrocele/spermatocele → observe; persistent symptomatic → elective repair
★ Varicocele with **infertility and abnormal semen**, pain, or adolescent testicular atrophy → consider repair

rows.label: Complications
items: Infertility, testicular atrophy; cancer metastasis to retroperitoneal nodes/lungs
Hydrocele may obscure tumor; treatment can impair fertility or endocrine function

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Orchiopexy for undescended testis** reduces infertility risk and facilitates examination; cancer risk persists
No routine population ultrasound or tumor-marker screening; promptly evaluate any new mass

rows.label: Mimics
items: Torsion: sudden severe pain, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex → urgent exploration
Inguinal hernia: reducible groin-continuous swelling, cough impulse
Epididymitis: tender posterior swelling, urinary/STI findings, increased Doppler flow

table.title: Benign examination patterns
rows: Cyst above/behind testis; separate, often transilluminates

scrotal-masses.evidence: Not checked online; established urologic localization and cancer-evaluation principles.

shoulder-pain.name: Shoulder pain
shoulder-pain.scope: Rotator cuff tendinopathy and tear, impingement, adhesive capsulitis, dislocation, biceps tendinopathy, glenohumeral osteoarthritis
shoulder-pain.core: Active versus passive range of motion, true weakness, trauma history, and pain location distinguish major shoulder disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Overhead work/sports, repetitive lifting, aging; fall or traction → acute structural injury
Diabetes, thyroid disease, prolonged immobilization → capsular fibrosis
Seizure/electrocution → posterior dislocation; anterior instability follows abduction/external rotation injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Lateral upper-arm pain often shoulder origin; radiation below elbow suggests cervical source
Night pain with preserved passive motion suggests cuff disease; weakness persisting after analgesia suggests tear
★ **Fever, hot joint, severe pain with any motion** → urgent septic arthritis evaluation
★ Deformity, absent pulse, deltoid numbness → dislocation with possible neurovascular injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tendon degeneration/tearing impairs dynamic stabilization; capsule contracture restricts joint excursion
Loss of articular cartilage causes mechanically painful glenohumeral degeneration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs** for trauma, arthritis, deformity; include axillary or scapular-Y view for dislocation
Compare strength, provocative tests, neck examination; document axillary nerve and distal pulses
Ultrasound or MRI for suspected tear, persistent symptoms, or surgical planning; avoid routine immediate MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Most atraumatic disorders → **activity modification, NSAIDs, physical therapy**; maintain motion
Selected painful tendinopathy/capsulitis → corticosteroid injection; avoid repeated injections into tendons
★ Dislocation → **prompt closed reduction**, brief sling, rehabilitation; recheck neurovascular function afterward
Acute traumatic full-thickness tear with functional loss → early orthopedic referral; severe OA → arthroplasty consideration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent instability, axillary nerve injury, greater-tuberosity fracture, persistent weakness
Prolonged sling use → stiffness; chronic massive tear → cuff arthropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rotator cuff/scapular strengthening, ergonomic changes, gradual return to overhead activity
Early supervised motion after injury when safe; avoid unnecessary immobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical radiculopathy: dermatomal symptoms, neck-provoked pain
ACS: exertional referred discomfort, diaphoresis, no motion-dependent localization
Pancoast tumor: smoking, hand weakness, Horner syndrome

table.title: Localizing examination
rows: Painful arc; positive Hawkins/Neer; strength preserved
Drop-arm or lag; objective resisted-movement weakness
Both active/passive motion limited, especially external rotation
Flattened deltoid; arm abducted, externally rotated
Anterior groove tenderness; pain with resisted supination

shoulder-pain.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAOS rotator cuff guideline 2025](https://www.aaos.org/quality/quality-programs/rotator-cuff/); other examination patterns established teaching.

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.name: Skin and soft tissue infections
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.scope: Cellulitis, erysipelas, folliculitis, furuncles, carbuncles, lymphangitis, necrotizing fasciitis
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.core: Skin infection management depends on purulence, systemic illness, and signs of deep tissue destruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin breaks, tinea pedis, edema/lymphedema, diabetes, obesity, injection drug use
Prior MRSA, crowding, recent hospitalization; surgery or penetrating trauma raises deep-infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Warmth, tenderness, erythema; rapidly expanding margins or systemic toxicity require urgent reassessment
★ **Pain out of proportion**, bullae, anesthesia, crepitus, shock → necrotizing infection
Perineal involvement → Fournier gangrene; saltwater exposure → Vibrio, freshwater → Aeromonas

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nonpurulent infection usually streptococcal; purulent lesions usually S aureus
Fascial spread and toxin-mediated injury → thrombosis, necrosis, sepsis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical diagnosis; **bedside ultrasound** if occult fluid collection suspected
Culture drained pus for severe, recurrent, or resistant infection; blood cultures for systemic toxicity
Suspected necrotizing disease → immediate surgical evaluation; imaging must not delay exploration
Low laboratory risk score or absent gas does not exclude necrotizing fasciitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Deep infection → **urgent debridement + vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam**, add clindamycin for toxin suppression
Confirmed group A streptococcal necrotizing infection → penicillin + clindamycin
Severe cellulitis/systemic illness → IV cefazolin; MRSA risk → vancomycin
★ Abscess: add **antibiotics** for systemic signs, immunocompromise, extensive disease, or failed drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, osteomyelitis, septic thrombophlebitis; tissue loss and amputation
Toxic shock, multiorgan failure; recurrent cellulitis worsens lymphatic dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat interdigital fungal infection, manage edema, skin hygiene, protect wounds
Recurrent staphylococcal infections → consider nasal mupirocin + chlorhexidine decolonization; avoid shared razors

rows.label: Mimics
items: Stasis dermatitis: chronic, often bilateral, itchy
DVT: deep swelling without superficial spreading infection; contact dermatitis: pruritic exposure-pattern rash

table.title: Superficial patterns
rows: Incision and drainage; TMP-SMX if needed

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established IDSA-based infection management.

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → shave, punch, or excisional biopsy deep enough to assess invasion
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
